Rigid Box Insert Types: Velvet, EVA Foam, Flocked or Paper Trays?

Published August 19, 2026 · Buyer guide · By BestPackFactory

Quick answer

Match the insert to the product: flocked EVA (0.8-2.0 mm) for cosmetics and electronics, velvet-covered greyboard for jewelry and watches, plain EVA or foam for heavy items, paper honeycomb or greyboard trays for light goods and recyclable claims. Insert cost adds roughly USD 0.10-0.80 per box depending on material and cut complexity. Tooling is usually included or USD 50-150 one-time; request a fit sample with your actual product before bulk.

Flocked EVA foam: the workhorse

Flocked EVA (0.8-2.0 mm skin over 10-30 mm density foam) is die-cut into slots, channels and cradles that grip products without scratching. It suits cosmetics, earbuds, chargers and small appliances. Specify slot width at product thickness plus 1-2 mm and slot depth at 60-80% of product height for secure retention. Ask for edge sealing on cut slots so flocking does not shed.

Velvet and PU-covered pads

Velvet over greyboard or foam gives the deepest luxury feel and is standard for jewelry, watches and fragrance. Cost is higher because covering is partly manual. Specify PU leatherette or velvet by texture and color match; request a 24-hour lightfastness check for white and cream velvets, which can yellow under UV display lighting.

Paper honeycomb and greyboard trays

Paper honeycomb bonded to greyboard holds light items and keeps the box curbside-recyclable in most markets. Greyboard trays (1.5-3.0 mm) with die-cut slots are the cheapest insert and work for foldable goods, books or bottled products. For shipping, honeycomb offers good crush resistance at low weight, but verify it under a 60-80 cm drop test rather than assuming.

How to spec the insert in an RFQ

Send the product drawing or sample, state the retention method (slot, cradle, full footprint), material preference and tolerance (usually ±1 mm). Ask the factory for a bare insert sample before the wrapped box sample, because insert fit errors are cheaper to fix at that stage. Include the insert in the same color-approval cycle as the box wrap.

Buyer checklist

  1. Choose insert material by product weight, fragility and brand positioning
  2. Specify slot width (product + 1-2 mm) and depth (60-80% of height)
  3. Request edge sealing or finishing on cut flocked slots
  4. Ask for a bare insert fit sample before the wrapped box sample
  5. Include insert cost and tooling in the per-unit comparison across suppliers

Frequently asked questions

Which insert is cheapest for a rigid box?

A die-cut greyboard tray is the lowest-cost option at roughly USD 0.08-0.25 per box. Paper honeycomb is similar and adds crush resistance; flocked EVA starts around USD 0.15-0.45 depending on depth and cut complexity.

When should we use velvet instead of flocked EVA?

Use velvet-covered pads for jewelry, watches and fragrance where the texture is part of the premium feel. Flocked EVA is the better value when the product is heavy, oddly shaped or needs deep cutouts.

Do inserts need separate tooling?

Most suppliers include steel-rule die tooling for inserts in the setup cost (roughly USD 50-150) or amortize it into the unit price. Ask explicitly whether tooling is charged once and whether it is reusable on reorders.

What the Spec Means for Buyers

Insert choice is a product-fit and cost decision. EVA foam at 20–60 density gives firm, die-cut cavities; paperboard trays are the economical printed option; molded pulp suits eco positioning; PET trays give clear product display; fabric pouches add a jewelry feel. All fit rigid boxes built from 1200/1500/1800 gsm greyboard wrapped in 157 gsm art paper or specialty papers, with corner gap ≤ 1.5 mm and lid-base fit 1.0–1.8 mm. The insert cavity is confirmed from your product dimensions on the free dieline. MOQ is 500 PCS.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which insert protects fragile items best?

EVA foam at 20–60 density provides firm, die-cut cavities that cradle the product during transit.

Can inserts be printed?

Yes — paperboard trays can carry printed branding; EVA, molded pulp and PET options are confirmed with the approved structure.
